name: New Voter ID Card (Form 6)
description: Complete guide to applying for a new Indian Voter ID card online on the Voters Service Portal. Includes Form 6 steps, document requirements, and BLO checks.

national.title: How to Apply for a New Voter ID Card Online (Form 6 - 2026)
national.summary: Step-by-step guide to applying for a first-time Voter ID card using Form 6 on the official Voters' Service Portal. Verified zero statutory fee, four annual qualifying dates, and complete document guidelines.

steps.title: Register and Log in on Voters' Service Portal
steps.description: Visit voters.eci.gov.in, sign up with your mobile number, and log in using password and OTP verification.
steps.calloutText: The Election Commission of India provides voter registration and physical EPIC cards 100% free of charge.

steps.title: Select 'Fill Form 6 - Register as a New Elector'
steps.description: Click on 'Form 6' designed for first-time voters turning 18 or citizens not yet registered in any electoral roll.

steps.title: Select State, District, and Assembly Constituency
steps.description: Choose your resident state, revenue district, and legislative assembly constituency where you currently reside.
steps.calloutText: Select the assembly constituency corresponding to where you currently sleep and live on a day-to-day basis.

steps.title: Enter Personal Details and Upload Passport Photograph
steps.description: Enter your first name, surname, and gender. Upload a recent color passport-size photograph with white background under 2 MB.

steps.title: Enter Relative Details and Contact Information
steps.description: Provide father's, mother's, or spouse's name. Enter your personal mobile number and active email address for OTP alerts.

steps.title: Fill Present Residential Address and Upload Address Proof
steps.description: Fill house number, street, locality, village/town, post office, and PIN code. Upload self-attested proof of residence.

steps.title: Fill Date of Birth and Upload Age Proof
steps.description: Enter exact date of birth and upload Aadhaar, birth certificate, or school marksheet as proof of age.
steps.calloutText: You can apply in advance if turning 18 before 1st Jan, 1st April, 1st July, or 1st Oct.

steps.title: Submit Declaration and Receive Application Reference Number
steps.description: Sign the online declaration and submit Form 6. Save your 16-character alphanumeric reference number to track your BLO verification.

documentRequirements.name: Proof of Date of Birth (PoB)
documentRequirements.description: Birth certificate, Aadhaar card, PAN card, driving licence, Indian passport, or class 10 school mark sheet.

documentRequirements.name: Proof of Ordinary Residence (PoA)
documentRequirements.description: Electricity, water, or gas bill (1 year), current bank passbook, Indian passport, or registered rent agreement.

documentRequirements.name: Passport Sized Color Photograph (4.5 cm x 3.5 cm)
documentRequirements.description: Recent frontal portrait photograph with a clean white background in JPEG format under 2 MB.

documentRequirements.name: Self-Declaration Form (For Applicants Aged 21+)
documentRequirements.description: Mandatory declaration stating that the applicant has not been enrolled in any other constituency previously.

documentRequirements.name: Family Member EPIC Number
documentRequirements.description: Voter ID card number of father, mother, or spouse who is already enrolled in the same electoral polling station.

rejectionReasons.title: Blurry or Incomplete Proof of Residence
rejectionReasons.description: Uploading an illegible utility bill or a cropped rent agreement causes the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) to reject.
rejectionReasons.solution: Upload a clean PDF showing the complete address matching the entry in Form 6.

rejectionReasons.title: Applicant Below 18 Years on All Four Qualifying Dates
rejectionReasons.description: Applying before attaining 18 on 1st January, April, July, or October of the current revision year leads to rejection.
rejectionReasons.solution: Submit Form 6 during the advance quarter when your 18th birthday falls on the upcoming qualifying date.

rejectionReasons.title: Dual Registration Across Multiple Assembly Constituencies
rejectionReasons.description: Holding an existing voter card in a hometown while applying fresh in a new city without Form 8 shifting is an offence.
rejectionReasons.solution: Use Form 8 for shifting residence instead of submitting a new Form 6.

rejectionReasons.title: Missing Family Member EPIC in Joint Household
rejectionReasons.description: Failing to mention a relative's EPIC number when other family members are already registered may trigger extra scrutiny.
rejectionReasons.solution: Provide your parent's or spouse's EPIC number in Section C to map your household to the correct polling booth.

rejectionReasons.title: Unverified Field Visit by Booth Level Officer (BLO)
rejectionReasons.description: If the BLO visits your residence during physical verification and neighbors state you do not live there, the form is rejected.
rejectionReasons.solution: Ensure your contact number is active and family members are aware of the upcoming BLO verification visit.

rejectionReasons.title: Selfie or Cropped Casual Photograph Uploaded
rejectionReasons.description: Photos with hats, dark sunglasses, filters, or busy colored backgrounds fail automated portrait verification.
rejectionReasons.solution: Upload a formal passport portrait with a plain white background taken in standard studio lighting.

faqItems.question: How much does a new Voter ID card cost in India?
faqItems.answer: A new Voter ID card is completely free. The Election Commission of India charges zero fee for Form 6 registration.

faqItems.question: What is the minimum age to apply for a new Voter ID card?
faqItems.answer: You can apply once you turn 18 years of age, or in advance if turning 18 in the upcoming quarter.

faqItems.question: What are the four qualifying dates for voter registration?
faqItems.answer: The four annual qualifying dates are 1st January, 1st April, 1st July, and 1st October.

faqItems.question: Can I download my Voter ID card online immediately?
faqItems.answer: Once your Form 6 is approved by the ERO, you can download your digital e-EPIC PDF immediately using OTP.

faqItems.question: What is the role of the Booth Level Officer (BLO) in Form 6?
faqItems.answer: The BLO conducts physical doorstep verification to confirm your identity and ordinary residence before electoral approval.

faqItems.question: Can I apply for a Voter ID if I live in a rented house?
faqItems.answer: Yes. A registered rent agreement or utility bill in your name or landlord NOC is accepted as address proof.

faqItems.question: How can I track the status of my Form 6 application?
faqItems.answer: Select 'Track Application Status' on voters.eci.gov.in and enter your 16-character acknowledgment reference number.

faqItems.question: Can an Indian citizen have Voter IDs in two different cities?
faqItems.answer: No. Registering in more than one constituency is a criminal offence under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act.
